prompt:
Write the lyrics of a hip-hop song about a night out in the city.

Write it as a working songwriter would, to be sung: lines that scan against a steady beat, a chorus that earns its repetition by meaning something slightly different each time it comes back, and verses that move a story forward through particular scenes, names, brands and street-level detail. Say the thing sideways: no line that states the feeling outright, no stock phrases, no word chosen only because it rhymes. Put one detail in each verse that only this story could contain.

Output only the lyrics, as plain lines with a blank line between sections: no title, no section labels, no chords, no commentary.
raw:
Cracked phone screen reads ten-fifteen
Weed smoke curls through the fire escape
Taxi’s a yellow wound across the bridge
Jasmine says my jacket’s a mistake

Pre-game in a kitchen with a flickering bulb
Tequila from a coffee mug pregnant with chips
Lucas palmed the aux cord like a dare
Now we’re shouting hooks with bitten lips

I hope the night forgets my name
I hope the DJ plays the thing we can’t request
I hope the floor gives way
And I wake up broke and blessed

Bouncer’s neck is thicker than a promise
His pat-down found Lucas’s tin of mints
Inside, the red light makes us all aquatic
A stranger grins with gold across his dent

Jasmine’s dancing like she’s shedding skin
Her drink is blue and tastes like second grade
Lucas mouths a secret to a man in vape exhaust
I guard the coats from everything they paid

I hope the night forgets my name
I hope the DJ plays the thing we can’t request
I hope the floor gives way
And I wake up broke and blessed

Spilled a bourbon on a pinstriped sleeve
The guy just laughed and ordered me a double
Turns out he frames the paintings at the Met
Says Vermeer’s the only one who understood the trouble

Jasmine lost an earring down a vent
We lit a match and watched the silver disappear
Lucas bought a rose from somebody’s date
And bit the stem and tucked it in my ear

I hope the night forgets my name
I hope the DJ plays the thing we can’t request
I hope the floor gives way
And I wake up broke and blessed

We ate cold empanadas on a stoop
The sky was pink and sick above the water towers
Lucas said the city’s just a sound that got too loud
And I could almost see the air around the hours

Jasmine took a photo of the three of us
Held the phone too high so all the streetlight screamed
Somebody’s pit bull licked the salt off of my hand
Nobody said a word. Nobody dreamed.
